expect.answer:
doc_status: success
— 18 extracted · 5 incorporated_by_reference
fixture: aapl-2025
routing: deterministic only — the escalation trigger stayed quiet, no tier ran, $0.0000 · 0 calls · 0 tokens

provenance:
M41. Live half of the inspector work, against `https://whaleforce-sec10k.zeabur.app` at `/api/meta` `git_sha` `6b37ffa99d05` (re-read at case-writing time, 2026-08-26). Hand-written plan, no LLM, $0.00 — `live`, like every other case in that suite. The start URL is the DEEP LINK the sec-10k-extract legibility row shipped (`?fixture=<id>&run=1` preloads the fixture select and extracts on load); a parameterised start URL is per-site data CLAUDE.md rule 6 allows, and nothing about the page's shape reaches `src/browser/`. Ground truth from the inspector's own `/api/extract/fixture` (rule 6's per-site ground-truth endpoint, eval side only, guarded by `sec10k-ground-truth-endpoint-eval-only`): `POST {"fixture":"aapl-2025"}` returns `doc_status: "success"` and `counts: {extracted: 18, incorporated_by_reference: 5}`, re-verified 2026-08-26.

TWO claims, and they point in opposite directions.
(1) `planner_saw.lacks: ["18 extracted"]` is the postmortem's shape S1, MEASURED AND STILL LIVE: the deep link removes the click, not the race. The observation the planner is given is taken right after `navigate()` returns (`domcontentloaded` plus a bounded wait for `load`), and the page's own extraction round-trip has not landed — the banner still reads "No filing extracted yet." So the deep link fixes S3 (no ambiguous button to press) and S2 (the banner is a named `status`), and does NOT fix S1. Measured 8/8 across the reps run while writing these two cases; the margin is physical rather than lucky — the observation lands ~0.3s after `load` and `POST /api/extract/fixture` alone measures 0.5–0.8s — but it is still a race, and this case is a receipt for one build of the target site (D28's expiry rule, which the postmortem §2 extends to the target's build too).
(2) The plan's own `navigate` step carries `expected_state: {text_visible: "fixture: aapl-2025"}`, which is ADR-027 Decision 2's "in mode B the existing authored `expected_state` path stands" — the settle-retry loop in `agent.check_state` (10 x 200ms) waits for the render, and the extraction then reads a settled page. The predicate names the fixture id from the START URL, not the answer: waiting on "doc_status: success" would have baked the expected value into the wait.

Watched RED first by deleting `expected_state` from the navigate step — the S4 shape with nothing authored to wait on. 3 reps, 3 non-answers and two different failure modes: two runs `success` with the answer `"Extracting…"` (a wrong-success shape a live run has no ground truth to catch — the D23 family), one run `failure:semantic`, `step 3 (extract): StepError: identity anchor 'aapl-2025' absent from the page the answer was read from`. Rep-level nondeterminism on an identical build, task and URL — T-M40-5-3's finding, reproduced on the one live site this project owns. The offline pin for that class already exists and is not duplicated here (`l4-shop-render-delayed`); a default post-click settle is M42's, not this milestone's.

Green 4/4 as committed. Task text is the first of the two the M41 block names verbatim. **Build provenance, corrected after cold review — three shas are involved and only two of them are the same thing.** `/api/meta` answered `5a44758598f5` when this milestone started and `6b37ffa99d05` at probe time. But the captured page's own footer — which the page fills from that same `/api/meta` field, one line of its own script — already read `build 6b37ffa99d05` in the FIRST capture, taken while `curl` to the same endpoint was still answering `5a44758598f5`. The two reads disagreed inside one session, which is what a rolling deploy across containers looks like; that explanation is INFERRED, not measured, and is written as an inference on purpose. What is measured: the committed snapshot is a capture of the build that reported itself as `6b37ffa99d05`, which is the same build ADR-030's probe ran against, so the fixture and the probe agree on one build rather than straddling two. The capture was re-taken later, after `/api/meta` had caught up, and diffed against the committed one — identical apart from a single `total_ms` figure inside the extraction evidence (227.6 -> 221.1), which is what that agreement looks like from the other side. The first version of this note claimed the capture was taken at `5a44758598f5`; the page says otherwise and the page is the artifact. Nothing in this repo reads either sha back — `tasks/TODO.md` T-M41-3 is the debt block for that, and D28's build-expiry rule is why it matters. **Target-build drift, 2026-08-28 (ADR-039's live run).** The inspector redeployed to `/api/meta` `git_sha` `573d30701852` and its `doc_status` region gained a fourth line — `routing: deterministic only — the escalation trigger stayed quiet, no tier ran, $0.0000 · 0 calls · 0 tokens` — so `expect.answer`, which is an exact match on the region's whole text, went red on both cases with `status success` and `planner_saw` still true: the verdict's `answer_matches` was the only check that moved. The figures this case actually cares about (`success`, 18/5) are unchanged and were re-read from `/api/extract/fixture` the same day. This is NOT a regression from ADR-039 — it is the target moving, which is the exact failure mode `tasks/TODO.md` T-M41-3 exists for and which nothing in this repo detects automatically; it surfaced only because ADR-039 had reason to run the `live` suite. The expected string is updated rather than loosened because there is no `answer_contains` key and inventing one to absorb a target's churn would weaken every case that uses it; D28's build-expiry rule already says what this string is a receipt for.

triage.note: This case measures the RESOLVER/EXECUTOR path on a real deployed page with a hand-written plan, like every other `live` case here — it says nothing about whether a real planner would author that `expected_state`. That question is what the ADR-030 deployment probe measures, and the two are reported separately in docs/support-matrix.md D30 rather than blended.
